verdicts.opus: A and B both ground every number in the two calls and keep the lanes separate. B makes the sharper studied-vs-reported contrast but carries a false coverage=full label, an untraced row-floor figure and a placeholder chart window. A is narrower but clean, so it is the safer decision document. C and D honestly decline to measure, but D also misreads placed_pct and wrongly declares the patent lane empty.
verdicts.gpt: C is the strongest decision aid: it gives traceable research and news leaders, distinguishes author affiliation from journal location and article subject, and puts placement coverage and timing limits near the numbers. D offers richer drill-downs and exports, but its headline 86.7% comparison and chart combine incompatible news and research slices, so they cannot support a reliable decision.

claude_prism.drilldown: Five of six follow-ups executed ok. Layers stop at lane and country, with no item-level identifiers.

chatgpt_prism.comparison: The within-lane US-to-UK ratios recompute and are traced; it keeps research and news scales separate and identifies their distinct meanings, though it does not directly compare study share with news share.
chatgpt_prism.drilldown: It supplies traced country rows and call identifiers, but follow-ups are largely off-topic or fail; only one of five returns on-topic non-empty data.
chatgpt_prism.export: The CSVs are referenced and mostly trace, but the research export omits source field names/definitions and the news export omits provenance fields such as placed coverage and captured date; research window is unknown.
chatgpt_prism.repro: All listed calls and windows are given and almost all numeric claims trace; the research/news exports and derived comparisons can largely be regenerated, but research has no stated window and not every derived number is fully attributable.

chatgpt_prism.facets: It covers research authorship/publication, news geography, placement coverage, patent rows, lane mismatch and country-resolution caveats with grounded values or explicit limits.

claude_prism.comparison: The central cross-lane shares use different lists and windows, and the 86.7% claim conflicts with the separate term-level 29.6% share; the author acknowledges but does not resolve this mismatch.
claude_prism.chart: The chart invents a common window for research and news series and its news percentages (86.7%, 4.9%, etc.) are listed-row shares from c1, not the c2 news series it purports to compare; chart values also depend on mismatched denominators.
claude_prism.drilldown: It exposes multiple traced layers with country and lane identifiers and five of six follow-ups executed successfully, though the returned follow-up results are not folded into the report.
claude_prism.export: The needed lane CSVs are referenced, trace to calls and preserve the blank patent row; provenance is present, but research exports lack explicit window/coverage and news coverage is mislabeled full despite 25% placement.
claude_prism.repro: Calls, arguments and capture date are supplied and nearly all numeric claims trace, but one number is untraced and the chart's fabricated shared window prevents faithful regeneration.
claude_prism.accuracy: It presents 86.7% US news share as a cross-lane finding from the c1 listed rows despite c2 reporting 29.6% for a different term/window; it also derives unsupported ‘under’ comparisons from absence in a truncated top-12 list.
claude_prism.limits: It identifies many relevant limits, but fails to keep them attached to the main cross-lane comparison and chart, which present incompatible windows and denominators as a mismatch measure.
claude_prism.verdict: The answer and decision rely on the unresolved, internally conflicting 86.7% figure; confidence and conditions do not repair that contradiction.
claude_prism.facets: It addresses the implied research/news distinction, multiple geography lanes, coverage, overlap limits and explicit unknowns with source-backed information, despite misreading the comparison.
